newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end zig-zag day with modest gains.
newsitem.headline: German shares end zig-zag day with modest gains.

text.p: German shares took their lead from a rebound on Wall Street in late afternoon European trade to post modest gains on Tuesday.
The 30-share IBIS DAX index ended the late electronic dealing session up 12.28 points at 3,761.07 points, some six points above the earlier DAX bourse trade closing level of 3,755.82.

After a day which sent prices spiralling to highs and lows in a 65-point range, the market took heart from a robust start on Wall Street, which had suffered a sharp decline on Monday when Japan's Prime Minister Ryuto Hashimoto commented on the potential sale by Japan of U.S. government securities.

But dealers noted that buying was extremely selective, focusing strongly on banking giant Deutsche Bank and electronics and engineering group Siemens, which leapt higher on strong technical buy signals.

"International investors do not appear to be interested in the German market right now," said one Frankfurt trader. "The action after the early selling pressure appears to be mainly from domestic investors looking for bargains."
Siemens ended late trade up 3.6 percent at 107.50 marks while Deutsche rose 4.4 percent to 101.85 marks. Fundamentals did not play a role in either share's gain, dealers said.
